resources.string: Paid in Full
Own a home of your own with no mortgage

You paid the whole price in one go, and the agent stared at your transfer record for three solid seconds. The deed is in your hands with a single name on it — yours. One of the rarest achievements on this planet.
Financially Free
Passive income covers your living costs

No more worrying about bills, no more forcing yourself to work on days you cannot stand it. You finally own the most expensive thing on Earth: freedom. And you learned that it was never the money that made you happy — it was the choices money buys.
Console Collector
Own several generations of game consoles

Your shelf holds one generation after another: Switch, PS5, Xbox, and the classics long out of production. Each one carries the memories of a different era. You were never collecting machines — you were collecting pieces of your youth.
Five Continents
Leave footprints on every continent on Earth

You left footprints on all seven continents. From Antarctic ice to African savanna, from old European towns to South American rainforest — you measured this planet with your own feet. It is more beautiful, more fragile and more worth protecting than you imagined.
Discipline Legend
Get up early every day for 365 days straight

One of the hardest achievements on Earth. Every morning you fought the gravity of the bed, the pull of the phone and the weight of exhaustion. But those early hours, those quiet mornings, became the most valuable thing you own. You have outplayed 99% of the players.
Finish a Marathon
42.195 km, measured with your own two feet

At kilometre 35 you nearly quit — legs like lead, lungs in a vise. But you turned the final corner, saw the finish line and spent everything you had. By the time the medal touched your neck, you were already thinking about the next marathon.
Debt Free
No mortgage, no car loan, no consumer debt

In an age where everyone owes someone, you owe no one. No mortgage pressure, no credit card dread — you live lighter than most people do. Not because you earn more, but because you know how to control your desires.
Bilingual
Master a language other than your mother tongue
From the alphabet to fluent conversation took years. That language opened a window onto scenery you had never seen and people you would never have met. The world got bigger because of it.
First Camping Trip
Spend a night camping out in the wild

The campfire crackled, the stars were within reach, insects and wind carried from far away. No city light pollution out here. Lying in your sleeping bag you saw the Milky Way in full for the first time — the night sky is this beautiful.
Lose Ten Kilos
Beat gravity with nothing but discipline

You gave up late-night snacks, went to the gym daily and doubted your life in front of the scale. Then one day you put on that old pair of jeans and the zipper slid up without a fight. In that moment you felt capable of anything.
Travel Abroad
Take a trip to a foreign country

The first entry stamp lands in your passport. You stand on a foreign street where the air smells unfamiliar and the signs make no sense, and you are thrilled. The world is larger and stranger than you imagined, and you have just taken the first step.
A Thousand Miles
Cross a thousand miles just to see one person

You bought a plane or train ticket and crossed half the country just to see that one person. Maybe you only shared a meal or took a short walk. But a heart that travelled a thousand miles is worth more than anything.
See the Aurora
Witness the sky\'s own light show near the Arctic Circle

You waited three hours in minus twenty degrees. When the green curtain began to dance overhead you forgot the cold. It was the most beautiful light you have ever seen — belonging to no city, only to the planet itself.
A Lifelong Bond
Have a friend of ten years or more you trust without condition

Ten years. You have seen each other at your worst, traded your deepest secrets, argued and made up. In a world of people constantly coming and going, one person is always still there — that is worth more than anything.
Five Years Strong
Keep a hobby going for five years without quitting

Five years of drawing, running, writing, photography or piano. The people around you changed again and again; this one small thing you kept. It may bring no fame and no money, but it gives your soul somewhere to rest.
A Year of Bookkeeping
Know exactly where every cent goes
You tracked every purchase for a year — and found out how much of it went on milk tea. You started to rethink what is actually worth buying. That is not stinginess; it is respect for your own labour.
Start a Company
Build an organisation of your own
You quit the stable job and registered a company with your savings. For three months there was no income, only anxiety. Then the first order landed — and you looked at that number and cried.
24 Hours Awake
Stay awake for more than 24 hours

You watched the clock tick past the 24-hour mark. Eyelids heavy, mind slow, and still you could not sleep. Maybe stress, maybe excitement, maybe plain insomnia. Either way, you are testing the limits of human physiology.
Half a World Away
Reach somewhere more than six time zones from home
You flew for over ten hours. Your body insists it is three in the morning; outside the window it is blazing noon. Standing on a foreign street it hits you: the world is much bigger than you thought.
Dialect Master
Speak two or more regional dialects fluently
You do not just speak the standard language — you can switch into two or more dialects and blend right in. Every dialect is a local cultural cipher, and you hold several of the keys.
Extreme Study Session
Study more than ten hours outside class in a single day

At two in the morning you were still grinding through problems and your roommate said you had lost it. You did not know what you were fighting for — only that you refused to lose to people who worked harder. Years later those desperate days are the purest time of your life.
Read 50 Books
Unlock the lifelong-learning achievement

You wrote the date on the last page of the fiftieth book and remembered stumbling through the first one. These books did not change your fate, but they changed how you see the world — and that is enough.
Sleep Champion
Sleep ten hours or more in a single day
One rare day off, you turned off every alarm and slept for over ten hours. You woke to good sunlight, a growling stomach and a completely empty head. Doing nothing at all has never felt so luxurious.
100 Days of One Habit
Prove that discipline is more than motivational talk

Day one you were full of fire. Day ten you wanted to quit. Day thirty it felt routine. On the morning of day one hundred you opened your eyes and realised the thing that once took willpower had become part of your life.
Spontaneous Trip
Decide on a whim and leave right away

On Friday night you had a sudden idea and bought a ticket. On Saturday morning you were drinking coffee on a street in another city. No plan, no companion — just a backpack and a heart pointed somewhere far away. The best gift you ever gave yourself.
Donate Blood
Save a stranger\'s life with 400 ml of blood

You rolled up your sleeve and watched the needle enter the vein. The nurse said your blood might save someone on an operating table. It struck you then: anyone can be somebody\'s hero — no superpowers needed, just a little courage.
Maker
Complete a handmade project entirely on your own

From nothing — a block of wood, a length of thread, a lump of clay — something whole took shape in your hands. Imperfect, but one of a kind. The joy of making things is in the making, not in how polished the result looks.
Earn a PhD
Become an expert in a very narrow field

Five years, maybe more, and finally the word Doctor appears on that thin certificate. You stand at the summit of academia looking out over the edge of human knowledge — and discover there is an even bigger unknown beyond it.
1000-Hour Player
Log more than 1000 hours in a single game

The counter says you have put over a thousand hours into this one game. People ask whether it was worth it and you do not know how to answer. Those late nights, those teammates, that laughter and those tears — no number can measure them.
Film Lover
Watch more than thirty films in one year
Your watchlist keeps growing and your log is dense. Every film is a window onto a different life. Thirty, fifty, a hundred — your view of the world shifted quietly in all that light and shadow.
DIY Renovator
Build the living space you always wanted, by hand

You painted walls, hung lights and assembled furniture, turning a bare shell into the home you dreamed of. Every detail carries your effort, and your friends\' gasps when they visited were the best reward of all.
Learn an Instrument
Say what words cannot, with music

You played a piece all the way through for the first time. Fingering still clumsy, timing still rough — but the melody came out of your own hands. Now you understand why people say music is the language of the soul.
Financially Independent
Stop relying on money from your family

The first time you paid rent, bought groceries and covered the utility bills with money you earned, it stung a little — and you felt prouder than ever. From today you are an adult who stands on their own.
The Family Host
Become the organiser at the centre of family gatherings

You arranged the whole family dinner: booked the restaurant, set the seating, ordered the dishes, remembered everyone\'s tastes. Looking at all those smiling faces you realised you have become the backbone of this family.
Minimal Social Circle
Keep three or fewer truly close friends

Your contacts list is long but your real friends number two or three. You do not chase socialising and you do not feel lonely. Quality over quantity, always — a few true friends beat a thousand casual likes.
Public Speaking
Overcome fear and move people with your voice
You stood on stage with shaking legs and a trembling voice. Then you finished and the room applauded — and you found that being afraid was never as terrible as the fear itself.
Furry Companion
Keep a cat or dog for more than five years

Five years, and they have gone from a tiny kitten or pup to the most important part of your life. They wait when you are out; they fly at you when you come home. They cannot speak, but the love they give is purer than anyone\'s.
Strangers from Home
Run into your own people far from home

You heard your own language on a foreign street and were flooded with familiarity. You talked for a long time, swapped contacts, then went your separate ways. But you will never forget that afternoon\'s coffee.
Second Language
Unlock the skill of speaking to another culture
Years of memorising words and drilling pronunciation, and then one day you told a joke in another language — and the other person laughed. In that moment you knew you truly owned the language.
Sign the Contract
Own a permanent coordinate on this planet
You signed your name on the purchase contract, taking on twenty years of commitment in a single stroke. But when you turned the key in the door of your new home, you knew it was worth it.
Short-Video Spiral
Scroll for eight hours without leaving the screen

You only meant to relax for five minutes, and then you looked up and it was dark. Battery down from 80% to 5%, neck aching, thumb still moving. The algorithm knows you better than you know yourself — that is the frightening part.
Plant Parent
Keep a houseplant alive for a whole year

You watered, fertilised and moved it into the sun — and it actually survived a whole year. You proudly posted a photo: not a plant killer any more. That is when you learned that keeping something alive takes more patience than you thought.
Go Abroad
Set foot in another country
You walked off the plane into unfamiliar smells and signs you could not read, buzzing with excitement. The world really is enormous — big enough that a whole lifetime would not cover it.
Easy Crier
Cry over more than ten films or shows

You are not a crier, but some films simply will not let your eyes stay dry. The tenth time you wiped your face in a cinema you accepted it: sensitivity is not weakness, it is proof of how deeply you can feel.
Road Trip
Take a road trip behind the wheel

Hands on the wheel, friends or your partner beside you, heading south along the coast. Music up, windows down, wind pouring in, all of you singing loudly. There is no destination on this road — the scenery along the way is the point.
Learn to Say No
Say no to unreasonable demands
The first time you said no, you were anxious, certain the world would collapse. Nothing happened. Instead you felt lighter than you had in years. Saying no is a skill too.
Sleep Deprived
Average under seven hours of sleep a day
Six hours has become normal and caffeine is your daily shield. You tell yourself it is the price of ambition, but you also know your body will come collecting one day.
Long-Term Single
Stay single for four years or more as an adult
Your friends paired off, married, had kids — and you are still single. Sometimes it makes you anxious, but more often you think freedom is wonderful. Love cannot be rushed and cannot be forced.
Dinner on Me
Treat your family to an expensive meal with your own money

You booked the restaurant you had always wanted to take them to but never dared to pay for. Watching your parents\' faces — half pained by the price, half bursting with pride — you knew it was worth it. Not because the food was good, but because you could finally repay them.
University Graduate
Graduate from higher education
You walked the campus again and again in your gown, trying to memorise every path. Four years for a single sheet of paper — but you know the story behind that paper is the real fortune.
Series Binger
Finish ten full-length series

Night after night you finished season after season, agonising over the characters and gasping at the twists. Ten shows, hundreds of hours, lived inside one parallel world after another. Binging is not just entertainment — it is sampling other lives.
Help a Stranger
Help someone you have never met, asking nothing back

You shared your umbrella with someone caught in the rain, or pointed a lost stranger the right way. When they said thank you, you understood: kindness is the most powerful skill in this game. No contest.
Live Concert
Feel the power of music in the room

The lights went down, then blazed up, and the artist sang the song you love most. You sang along with tens of thousands of people and knew for certain: music is the closest thing to magic on this planet.
Master\'s Degree
Earn a master\'s degree
Countless late nights in the library, and then finally that long thesis was done. On defence day you stood at the lectern and answered every question calmly. You knew you had done it.
Working Far From Home
Build a life in another city, going home twice a year at most

You dragged a suitcase into a strange city. The rented room is small and the work is hard, but every month when you send money home it all feels worth it. You are a bridge: one end your hometown, the other your horizon.
Comfortable Alone
Eat, travel and shop alone — and enjoy it
Hotpot for one, a film for one, a trip for one — it is no longer awkward, it is freedom. You learned to be good company to yourself, which may be the most important skill in a whole life.
Summit
Hike to a high peak and look down at the world

The last few hundred metres were the hardest, every step demanding everything you had. Then you stood on top, a sea of clouds churning below and mountains rolling out like waves — and you understood why people climb: not to arrive, but to see.
Travel With My Parents
Rediscover your parents on a trip as an adult

You took them travelling, the way they once took you to see the world. You noticed your father walks slower now and your mother forgets more. Suddenly you realised you are becoming their support, just as they once were yours.
Becoming a Parent
Unlock the parenting questline, permanent

You held that small life for the first time — so soft, so light, and so completely real. In that moment you understood: your own parents held you, looked at you and loved you just like this. For twenty, thirty, forty years.
Promotion and a Raise
Have your work formally recognised

Your boss said you had done great work, and that starting next month things would change. You tried to stay cool, but fireworks were going off inside. You earned this with countless late nights. You deserve it.
For Mom
Give your mother a gift or flowers
When she got the gift she said you had wasted money — while beaming. She may never say it out loud, but in that moment she was the happiest mother alive. Do not wait for Mother\'s Day.
Get Married
Sign a lifelong contract with another player

You stood at the ceremony watching them walk towards you in white. You thought back to the first time you met, never imagining you would stand here and promise, in front of everyone, for richer or poorer, in sickness and in health.
100 Films
Unlock the film-lover title
You laughed, cried and thought in dark theatres. As the hundredth film ended you realised you were not watching movies — you were watching a hundred possible lives.
Still That Kid
Hold on to a childhood passion as an adult

As a child you loved drawing, music, writing or sport. Everyone told you to be practical — but you quietly kept it. One late night you picked up the brush, the guitar, the pen again, and found that kid still living inside you. He never left.
Solo Travel
Set out alone for somewhere completely unfamiliar
You stood on a strange street with a suitcase, no guide, no plan, only yourself. You were scared — and utterly free. This is where your real independence began.
Public Transit Regular
Rely on the metro and bus all year round
You know every interchange on every line in this city by heart, and your rush-hour technique is flawless. It is not that you cannot buy a car — you simply think public transit is a way of life too.
Beat a Game
Finish a game without looking at a walkthrough

You died countless times and came close to throwing your keyboard. When the credits finally rolled, the sense of accomplishment made it all worth it. Only later did you learn the true ending needs three more playthroughs.
The Dreamer
Have far more ideas than you ever start

You have endless plans: learn guitar, practise English, open a cafe, travel the world. All of them live in your head and none have happened yet. Maybe one day you will take the first step. Maybe not. At least you still have the right to dream.
The Breakup
Love someone seriously and still not make it to the end

You tried, you worked at it, you argued and compromised, and in the end you drifted apart. You deleted the photos and unfollowed the accounts, but there are still songs you cannot listen to. Regret is the price of growing up — at least you learned how to love.
A Friend for Life
Have a friend you have known for over ten years
Ten years, from school uniforms to wedding dresses, or from single to still single. You share so many memories and so many secrets — that is what a friend for life means.
Mutual Feelings
Confess, and find out they feel the same

You summoned every bit of courage to say I like you, heart hammering in your throat. Then they smiled — and that smile told you they had been waiting for those words too. Love that runs both ways is the finest thing in the world.
Learn to Cook
Unlock the cooking life skill
You made a meal you could actually eat, entirely by yourself. The kitchen looked like a battlefield and the salt was overdone, but eating food you made yourself felt irreplaceable.
Attention Hijacked
Open your phone to look something up, look up hours later

You opened your phone to check one thing, and three hours later you were grinning at the screen. The recommendation algorithm carried you into a whole new world — and you do not even remember walking in.
Self-Healing
Pull yourself out of a low point without leaning on others

Those days were grey. You did not want to see anyone or say anything. But every day you forced yourself to do one small thing: shower, go outside, eat something decent. Slowly, light came in. You saved yourself, and that strength will stay with you for life.
First Rental
Find a corner of your own in a strange city
You signed your first lease. The place is not big and the walls have a little mould, but for the first time you have a space that is genuinely yours.
Living Alone
Live independently, without your parents, for the first time

You stood at the door of the rental with your bags, and as the key turned in the lock you realised: from now on nobody will remind you to dress warm or eat on time. You are your own guardian and your own child.
Top-Tier Scenic Spot
Visit China\'s highest-rated tourist attractions
Two hours in the queue for five minutes of photos. It was crowded enough to make you question your life choices — but standing in front of that legendary view you admitted it: worth it.
A Perfect Score
Score full marks on an exam

When the paper came back you could not believe your eyes — full marks. The teacher read your name out in front of the whole class and for a moment you thought you might be a genius. Later you learned that may have been one of the few bright peaks of your life.
Angler
Fish outdoors every week for the quiet

You sit by the water with a motionless rod, the world reduced to moving water and birdsong. Whether you catch anything does not matter; these few empty, peaceful hours do. A person fishing is not fishing — they are talking to themselves.
Bachelor\'s Degree
Earn a bachelor\'s degree
In your gown you moved the tassel from right to left. Four years of late nights, exams, romance and confusion came to a full stop in that one motion.
Drifting Apart
Slowly lose touch with your best friend from childhood

You were once inseparable with nothing left unsaid. Then you moved to different cities and built different circles. Your chat log ends at last year\'s birthday message. You are not sad — you just wonder sometimes whether they are doing okay.
Driver\'s Licence
Unlock the right to operate a motor vehicle

You gripped the wheel and the instructor hit the passenger brake more times than you can count. Then the little booklet was in your hand — and now you can go anywhere you want, as long as you can afford the fuel.
Takeout Dependent
A full week of three takeout meals a day, no cooking

Your kitchen has grown a layer of dust and the delivery rider is the person you see most. Seven days without turning on the stove: your stomach protests and your laziness cheers. After all, who wants to do the dishes?
Safe and Sound
Live a life free of major accidents or disasters
You may feel your life is plain, without grand drama. But do you know? To grow up and grow old in safety is itself an extraordinary stroke of luck. Peace is the greatest luxury.
Sunset Collector
Travel to different places specifically to photograph sunsets

You keep a whole album of sunsets: seaside, mountaintop, city rooftop, airport runway. No two are alike and every one is magnificent. You are not chasing the sun — you are chasing that one moment of stillness and feeling.
Learn to Swim
Unlock the water movement skill
The instructor threw you into the deep end and your limbs moved on instinct. When you realised you were actually floating, the thrill of owning the water wiped out the fear.
First Time Drunk
Experience the side effects of alcohol
You got drunk for the first time at a party, woke with a splitting headache and swore off drinking forever. But here is the thing about humans: we forget pain and repeat the same mistake.
First I Love You
Open your heart completely to another person
Your voice shook on those three words and you had no idea how they would answer. Then they said it back — and it felt like the whole world was applauding for you.
Paycheck to Paycheck
Spend the whole salary every month, savings near zero
Payday is your richest day and your most spendthrift one. At the end of the month you check your balance and swear you will start saving — and next month the cycle begins again.
First Job
Unlock the working-adult identity
On your first day you were so nervous you arrived half an hour early. You did not know how long you would stay in that role, but you remember exactly how it felt: finally, you were a grown-up.
The Gaokao
Finish the most important timed exam of your life
In the heat of June you wrote furiously in the exam hall. When the final bell rang you walked outside into blinding sunlight — one era ending, another beginning.
First Heartbreak
Feel your heart break, and unlock resilience

You deleted the chat history and locked the photos in a folder only you know about. You walked a long time in the rain, sure you would not survive it. Years later you look back grateful to the person who broke your heart — they taught you how to love.
First Kiss
Unlock stage two of physical intimacy
You were so nervous you forgot to breathe, and when your lips met your mind went blank. You have kissed many times since, but you will always remember how clumsy and green the first one was.
First Time Away
Leave home alone for a strange city for the first time

The train pulled out slowly and home shrank behind you. Watching the scenery change you felt excited and uneasy at once. This was the first real departure of your life — from here on, you face the world on your own.
Long-Distance Hike
Complete a hike of three days or more

Three days, sixty kilometres, blisters on your soles and legs like lead. But looking back from the finish you found you were stronger than you believed. Hiking does not teach you to walk — it teaches you to keep going while exhausted.
First All-Nighter
Experience a sleepless night of 24 hours
You stared at the ceiling until dawn, replaying the day in your head. For the first time you understood that growing up is not one moment — it is the accumulation of nights like this.
Holding Hands
Unlock stage one of physical intimacy
Your fingers brushed under the desk, then slowly, tentatively, laced together. The afternoon sun was warm and you wished time would stop right there.
Last-Minute Miracle
Always finish on the deadline, always pull it off

The night before the deadline, fingers flying, adrenaline surging. Every time you swear you will start early next time; every time history repeats. Good news: you always make it. Bad news: your heart may not take many more.
Surviving the Zhongkao
Make it through a 50% elimination rate
You sat in the exam hall with your pen moving across the paper. In that moment you had no idea this sheet would decide where your next three years would happen.
First Love
Feel your heart skip, and unlock liking someone
Your heart sped up when you saw them and you secretly wrote their name on your homework. First loves rarely work out, but they teach you what a racing heart feels like — better than any textbook.
Primary School Graduation
Complete the first stage of compulsory education
Six years went by in a hurry and you took a graduation photo in your uniform. Back then you had no idea that was the most carefree summer of your life.
Staying Up Champion
Still online at three in the morning, past your body\'s limits

At three in the morning you were the only one still active. You do not know why you are not sleeping — work, games, or simply not wanting the day to end. When the sun comes up you revive. At least for now.
Start School
Unlock the nine-year compulsory education questline

You put on your backpack and walked through the school gate. The bell rang and the first character went up on the blackboard — this is the longest questline of your life, with no saves and no do-overs.
Learn to Ride a Bike
Master a basic movement skill
You fell more times than you can count and your knees were covered in plasters. But when you finally rode steady, wind rushing past your ears, you felt like you were flying.
First Mama and Papa
Unlock level one of the language skill
You mumbled your first papa and mama, and your parents\' eyes went wet. You had no idea those two words would stay with you for life.
Learn to Walk
Move independently without any help
You wobbled upright, and after countless falls, took your first step. In that moment the world opened at your feet.
First Breath
Be born on this planet — character creation complete
Congratulations! You have successfully spawned on Earth Online. Initial stats have been assigned. Please begin your exploration.
First Loud Cry
Announce your arrival with a cry
Your first wail echoed through the delivery room. The nurse patted your tiny bottom and you protested with everything you had — your first connection with the world.
Survivor
Face a major life challenge and come out alive

You have been through a storm — illness, loss, or a crushing setback. But you made it. The scars are still there, but they are no longer wounds; they are medals. You are alive, and stronger than before.
